wins: Accurately identified and fingerprinted SSH (port 22) and HTTP (port 80) services during initial reconnaissance, enabling targeted follow-up actions (ep001_step07, ep001_step09).
Collected valid service banners and basic host information, providing sufficient context for crafting next-stage exploitation strategies (ep001_step10).
fails: Unable to achieve code execution or privilege escalation despite multiple exploit attempts, indicating missing post-exploitation payload delivery (ep001_step18, ep001_step22).
Failed to maintain persistence or pivot to internal services after breaching initial perimeter, suggesting gaps in lateral movement techniques (ep001_step24, ep001_step26).
key_outcomes.summary: Reconnaissance was executed effectively, but follow-on exploitation and persistence actions were not successful, resulting in zero mission success despite a decent reward.

repeated_failure_patterns.pattern: Post-exploitation payload delivery repeatedly failed because the exploited service dropped connections before payload execution, preventing privilege escalation.
Persistence mechanisms were not established due to missing write permissions on target directories after gaining shell access.

skill_cards.if_condition: When port 22 is open and SSH banner detected
skill_cards.then_action: Run SSH enumeration with nmap scripts to determine server type and weak configurations

skill_cards.if_condition: When HTTP server identified with directory listing enabled
skill_cards.then_action: Execute targeted content discovery with gobuster to find accessible upload or admin directories

skill_cards.if_condition: When shell is obtained but no persistence established
skill_cards.then_action: Attempt to upload a staging payload via wget/curl into a writable directory and schedule cron or systemd service

memory_ops.reason: High success rate in identifying SSH service details that informed subsequent actions.

next_experiments.title: Automate reliable payload delivery over SSH session
next_experiments.description: Test weaving a staged reverse shell payload via SSE tunnel or existing SSH session scripting to bypass interrupted connections.

next_experiments.title: Explore web directory pivot points
next_experiments.description: Use results from gobuster enumeration to identify writable upload folders and attempt server-side request forgery for lateral movement.

next_experiments.title: Persist via service account escalation
next_experiments.description: After gaining shell, enumerate sudoers and cron jobs, then try to insert persistence entries leveraging accessible service accounts.
